events.title: Atahualpa Is Captured at Cajamarca
events.description: The Inca ruler Atahualpa was seized by Francisco Pizarro and a small band of Spanish conquistadors at Cajamarca, in what is now Peru. The Spaniards ambushed him in the middle of a meeting.
events.significance: The capture of Atahualpa opened the way for Spain to conquer the Inca Empire, one of the largest states in the Americas.

events.title: Gustavus Adolphus Dies at Lützen
events.description: Swedish forces defeated an imperial army under Albrecht von Wallenstein at the Battle of Lützen during the Thirty Years' War. Their king, Gustavus Adolphus, was killed in the fighting.
events.significance: The loss of one of Europe's most admired military leaders changed the course of the war. Sweden had risen to become a major power under his rule.

events.title: The Suez Canal Opens
events.description: The Suez Canal officially opened to shipping. It linked the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea across Egypt.
events.significance: The canal cut thousands of miles from sea routes between Europe and Asia and reshaped global trade.

events.title: Oklahoma Becomes the 46th State
events.description: Oklahoma was admitted to the United States as the 46th state. It was formed by merging Oklahoma Territory with Indian Territory.
events.significance: Statehood ended the separate Indian Territory and marked a major turning point for the region's Native American nations.
